# Interaction design

## Directives

No directive is in force at this node.

## Definition

The design of how an interface responds when people act on it: which controls appear, in what order, and what happens next.

## References

- You choose the size or the position of a button, a link, or a menu. Read [Fitts's law](fitts-law.md).
- You choose the number of options in a menu, a step, or a first screen. Read [Hick's law](hicks-law.md).
- You design how people move between screens. Read [Navigation](navigation.md).
- You choose which options appear first. Read [Progressive disclosure](progressive-disclosure.md).
- You design feedback, an exit, a confirmation, an error message, or help. Read [Usability heuristics](usability-heuristics.md).
